title.narrative: Providing critical WASH, education and protection services to people affected by Typhoon Yagi in Lào Cai and Yên Bái Provinces

description.narrative: UNICEF will provide life-saving support in the WASH and Education sectors (with a strong protection focus) in the most affected districts of Yên Bái and Lào Cai provinces in Viet Nam. In Yên Bái, the targeted areas are Yên Bình and Lục Yên districts, while in Lào Cai, the focus is on Bắc Hà and Mường Khương districts. These regions were severely impacted by flooding, landslides, and high winds following Typhoon Yagi, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities. In Yên Bái, the targeted communes have a poverty rate exceeding 35 per cent, significantly higher than the national average of 4.7 per cent. Before the typhoon, only 9.5 per cent of people in these areas had access to safe drinking water, much lower than the national average of 52 per cent. UNICEF’s WASH activities will include provision of WASH supplies to affected households, repair of piped water systems, conduct of WASH behavior change communication activities, provision of WASH supplies to affected schools and healthcare facilities, repair of WASH facilities in eight schools and three healthcare facilities. All activities will be implemented through the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD), with consultant support for technical assistance, implementation, and monitoring. The project will target 21,839 people with safe WASH behaviors, and 7,200 people with critical WASH supplies, as well as 2,400 children with basic WASH facilities at school or learning facilities. Three healthcare facilities will have their WASH facilities repaired. In the Education Sector, UNICEF will implement activities aiming to restore access to quality education while addressing critical protection needs in the aftermath of the disaster. The response will focus on providing essential teaching and learning materials and other school supplies to ensure 8,000 children can continue learning without further disruption. To support affected families, UNICEF will also conduct multipurpose cash (MPC) transfers through a "cash plus" approach, which will provide additional services to address broader needs like child protection and well-being.In addition to material support, UNICEF will prioritize the mental health and psychosocial well-being of students and teachers by providing Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). This will be integrated with teacher training focused on PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse), gender-based violence (SRGBV), and social-emotional learning (SEL). These initiatives will help equip teachers and school administrators with the necessary skills to create safe, supportive environments for students, while also fostering essential transferable skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, and resilience-building in children.UNICEF’s WASH and education interventions in Yên Bái and Lào Cai provinces will deliver essential support to communities hit hardest by the disaster. By integrating PSEA, GBV prevention, disability inclusion, and protection across all activities, the response ensures that vulnerable groups, especially children are at the center of response efforts. This approach not only meets immediate needs but also builds resilience, creating safer, more inclusive environments for families as they rebuild their lives.
